en: The Śāriputra Dhāraṇī Sūtra, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Saṃghabara of Funan during the Liang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Mahāvana Monastery in the kingdom of Vaiśālī, together with...
He was accompanied by a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus.
At that time, the Buddha reflected that three months hence he would enter parinirvāṇa.
He then addressed the Elder Maudgalyāyana:
"You must go to a thousandfold world-system and inform the community of bhikṣus to come to the Buddha's presence."
At that time, Maudgalyāyana, having received the Buddha’s instructions,
reached the summit of Mount Sumeru in a single thought-moment and uttered a great sound that proclaimed throughout a thousandfold world system.
At that time, there was an assembly of four hundred million bhikṣus at the Mahāvana Vihāra.
They all went to where the Buddha was, prostrated at his feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that moment, the Elder Śāriputra contemplated with single-minded concentration.
"I shall, by means of my supernormal powers,
cause all those places throughout the trichiliocosm where there are assemblies of bhikṣus to gather here at this Great Forest Monastery."
Immediately, by means of his supernormal powers,
he caused the assemblies of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas throughout the trichiliocosm to gather together at once.
Having arrived, they prostrated at the Buddha’s feet.
At that time, in a single moment of thought, the World-Honored One addressed the bodhisattvas.
Their names were Bodhisattva Sudarśana,
Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, and Bodhisattva Apāyajah.
The Bodhisattva Severing Darkness;
the Bodhisattva Who Has Transcended All Realms;
the Bodhisattva Subduing All Veils.
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva,
Gandhahastin Bodhisattva,
and Pratibhānakūṭa Bodhisattva.
Maitreya Bodhisattva,
noble son, you shall go to the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
where there are bodhisattvas who are in their last birth before attaining enlightenment (ekajātipratibaddha).
"O you who are bodhisattvas of non-retrogression,
and you who have already attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti), you should all be universally summoned to assemble here."
At that time, when the bodhisattvas heard these words of the Buddha,
they replied, "Excellent, excellent!
and immediately accepted the instruction.
In a single moment,
by means of his supernormal powers, he gathered all the bodhisattvas from as many Buddha-worlds in the ten directions as there are sands in the Ganges River,
and they all assembled here at this Great Forest Monastery.
There were one hundred thousand three million billion nayutas of bodhisattvas in their final birth before enlightenment (ekajātipratibaddha) and those who are non-regressive (avaivartika).
There were bodhisattvas who had already attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*),
bodhisattvas in their final birth (*ekajāti-pratibaddha*) numbering in the hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas,
and bodhisattvas who had not regressed from the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena numbering three hundred trillion nayutas.
They all assembled together, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit on one side.
At that time, Śāriputra saw the great assembly of bodhisattvas with single-minded concentration, and thought:
"I shall now inquire of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, regarding a Dharma not yet heard."
By virtue of this question, all bodhisattvas shall attain freedom from doubt,
shall be without hindrance, and shall possess the wisdom of eloquence;
they shall hear the Dharma being preached by the Buddhas of worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Until they attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*,
they will constantly remember their past lives and shall obtain the four kinds of purity of a bodhisattva.
What are the four? They are:
the purity of sentient beings and the purity of phenomena.
They delight in eloquent speech and attain the purity of the Buddha-field.
Furthermore, they obtain four sublime and excellent dharmas. What are these four?
Excellence of body, excellence of speech, excellence of mind, and excellence of birthplace.
Furthermore, one attains entry into four kinds of dhāraṇī-doors. What are these four?
That is to say: the dharani-door of inexhaustible upholding;
the dharani-door of skillful means for entering the faculties of sentient beings;
and the dharani-door of unimpeded skillful means regarding karmic retribution.
Regarding the dharani-door of the profound patience of dharmas, he questioned [the Buddha] in succession according to his reflections, like a precious maṇi jewel.
He addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
I now wish to pose questions in succession so that the virtuous conduct of all bodhisattvas may be purified.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain this for me.
The Buddha told Śāriputra: "If all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas wish to reach all dharmas without attachment,
they should recite this mantra."
Śūṇi śūṃ maṃ sa vaṃ ta muṃ.
Yudini yudini rudiparāvi he li karoṣa karoṣa.
Sīrī brāhmaṇapati khilā khili.
He-li, He-li-lie, He-lo.
Kṣī-jiè wú-yīn dǐ-chā pó-mí (kṣīty-ācāpami)
Cala calane atati arane.
Nimade nimavate nirdhaye tiṣṭha.
Nihale bimale śubhe brahmani ṭiṭṭibhe pade pāpe vihāpade.
Vāsaṃkhyeya-damī-vipulaḥ
Bharavī saṃkarāliśade dide dide mahādide yaśapadisañcare.
Acāle macāle pamacāle.
Dhiti dhiti svāhā | asaṃgavihāre asaṃganirhāre |
Nihāravimale nihāraśubhe nidhitarakṣami.
Sthāmi sthāma-pati mahā-pariṣad-saman.
Tāvaravī vipulapāravī vipula raiśami śarada mukhi sarvatārā anugati āna.
*Ji-di-tuo-luo-ni tuo-luo-ni ni-da-duo-ju-di-le sō-hē*.
Śāriputra, if there is a bodhisattva who practices this dhāraṇī mantra...
One does not conceive of conditioned or unconditioned phenomena;
one does not speak of these phenomena, does not contemplate these phenomena,
does not cling to these phenomena, and does not construct these phenomena.
One does not act for the sake of attaining this dharma nor for the sake of abandoning this dharma;
one does not act for the sake of increasing or decreasing, nor does one perceive dharmas that are associated or dissociated;
one does not perceive arising or ceasing, nor does one perceive the three periods of time.
One does not perceive the nature of retrogression, nor does one perceive the nature of gathering or dispersing.
There is nothing to be taught; one practices only the mindfulness of the Buddha.
One does not dwell on form, nor on the primary and secondary marks, nor on that which is not the primary or secondary marks.
One does not dwell on precepts nor dwell on non-precepts.
The same applies to concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation.
One does not dwell on caste, nor on friends, relatives, or kinsmen.
Regarding abodes and non-abodes, as well as attainment and non-attainment,
one does not discriminate among the aggregates, elements, or sense bases;
one does not conceptualize wisdom or the absence of wisdom.
One does not dwell on the purity of self or others;
one does not dwell on the purity of sentient beings or the non-purity of sentient beings;
one acts neither for one's own sake nor for the sake of others.
One does not dwell on the purity of the three karmas,
nor does one dwell on the purity of present or future conduct.
Śāriputra, this is what is called "recollection of the Buddha."

It is called "Entering All Dharmas by Grasping Their Names," it is called "The Dharani of Skillful Means for Attaining the Practice of All Dharmas," and it is also called "Cultivating the Ultimate Truth."
It is also called "fulfilling what is desired.
This samādhi is termed "exclusively for the attainment of bodhi," and it is also called "the nature of the Dharma-treasury, which is the cultivation of all roots of goodness not dependent on others."
It is also called the Dharani of Concealing the Marks and Signs;
it is also called the Dharani of Seeking Skillful Means;
it is also called the Dharani of Crossing Over Mara.
Śāriputra, this dhāraṇī consists of boundless practices and vows.
If bodhisattvas of the future attain its meaning,
they will achieve non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
One shall swiftly attain the unsurpassed path.
Why is this? Because this is the treasury of merit of all Buddhas;
this is the discernment of the conduct of all sentient beings.
Therefore, this dhāraṇī is called "The Practice of Non-Apprehension.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"Do not take pleasure in or become attached to the emptiness of all phenomena."
Regarding the enlightenment of all Buddhas, do not give rise to discrimination;
do not calculate whether all phenomena have faults or are faultless.
If one can practice in this way, one will swiftly attain dhāraṇī.
Hearing this sutra, which is inexhaustible and never extinguished,
and cultivating the equipment for wisdom, one shall attain the unsurpassed path.
A bodhisattva who upholds this dharani-dharma-gate—
One is able to hear the subtle and wondrous teachings spoken by the Buddhas of the ten directions;
subsequently, one comes to know the foremost Dharma— the meaning of its words and phrases—
as the light of the sun and moon, which shines everywhere without exception.
The Bodhisattva thoroughly understands all phenomena, and their characteristics are likewise so.
This gateway of dhāraṇī encompasses all phenomena;
for sentient beings who have doubts, it provides answers to all questions and difficulties.
Those who uphold this dhāraṇī are all able to explain this bodhisattva wisdom;
they never suffer any decline or diminution.
These are the true sons of the Buddha, who shall swiftly attain supreme enlightenment.
Those who uphold this dhāraṇī are remembered by all Buddhas and are respected by all sentient beings; because they uphold this dhāraṇī,
they are able to manifest their bodies so as to be seen by eight thousand million billion Buddhas.
Touched by the hands of all Buddhas, they are comforted and brought to peace;
even in a single day and month, they can receive and uphold this dhāraṇī,
whereby all sins committed throughout billions of kalpas are entirely extinguished.
Having cultivated all manner of meritorious virtues throughout incalculable eons,
the merit of this Ekādaśamukha-dhāraṇī is equal to that of all the devas and māras; none can obstruct it.
By upholding this dhāraṇī, one is able to maintain and retain all the dharmas of the Buddhas, including the merits of meditative concentration and wisdom;
it is called the "Gate of Dhāraṇīs," and there are those who possess resolute faith in it.
In a future age, you shall surely attain the Unsurpassed Way;
because you heard this dhāraṇī from the Buddha Dīpaṃkara in the past,
you were prophesied by all the Buddhas to achieve enlightenment under the name Dīpaṃkara.
It is joyful to behold Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in a single thought-moment;
it is also joyful to know the teachings spoken by all Buddhas throughout the ten directions,
to uphold the dhāraṇīs, and to fully attain the fruits one desires.
Such a person will surely possess power; they purify all Buddha-fields, their radiance, and their marks and signs.
All matters are fully perfected, yet they are signless and without attachment, seeking no further karmic retribution.
I only pray that you and all sentient beings may swiftly attain the unsurpassed path;
therefore, today you should practice with diligence and listen attentively,
for in the future you will certainly attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"If a bodhisattva accomplishes four dharmas, they shall attain dhāraṇī. What are these four?"
They take no pleasure in sensual desires,
are free from envy,
and are able to relinquish everything for the sake of all sentient beings.
Day and night, they contemplate all phenomena without affliction or anger.
Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva accomplishes these four dharmas, they shall attain this dhāraṇī.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses (geya):
Lust and envy are the dharmas of Māra; those who would enter the path to hell should abandon them.
Regarding both wealth and the Dharma, one should practice giving to all beings and contemplate day and night so as not to give rise to vexation or anger. If one can act in this way—
On attaining the dhāraṇī: Furthermore, Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva accomplishes four dharmas, they attain this dhāraṇī. What are these four?
They practice the conduct of an araṇya-dweller,
maintain profound dharmakṣānti,
and take no pleasure in gain, offerings, or fame.
A bodhisattva who is able to relinquish all things received, even at the cost of their own body and life, achieves dharani by accomplishing these four dharmas.
The Buddha spoke this geya:
Practicing in the araṇya, praised by virtuous people,
with body and mind tranquil and unmoving, always dwelling in the forest,
burning away negligence as if setting one's head on fire, one gives rise to the profound patience of the Dharma.
Regarding fame and gain, he is entirely without attachment;
with a pure and untainted mind, he seeks the unsurpassed path.
He is able to relinquish all that is most cherished—wife, children, and even his own life.
Without giving rise to a mind of regret or stinginess, one will ultimately return to extinction;
the Bodhisattva, through diligent vigor, cultivates these four superior practices and,
like the aforementioned dhāraṇī, will surely attain them before long.
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
if a bodhisattva accomplishes four dharmas, they will obtain this dhāraṇī. What are these four?
Regarding the meaning of the entry into the eight syllables: what are the eight syllables?
The syllable *va* enters into the meaning that all phenomena are without self (*anātman*).
The syllable *ra* enters into the meaning of the Dharma-body, which possesses marks and signs yet is itself without marks or signs.
The syllable *sa* enters into two meanings: the dharma of the foolish and the dharma of the wise.
The syllable *ja* enters into the meaning of birth, old age, sickness, and death, as well as non-birth, non-aging, non-sickness, non-death, non-arising, and non-ceasing.
The syllable *ka* enters the meaning of the karmic retribution of the stage of completing one's practice;
the syllable *tha* enters the meaning of the dharma-stage of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness through the dhāraṇī of upholding;
the syllable *sa* refers to śamatha and vipaśyanā.
Śamatha-vipaśyanā refers to entering into the meaning of all dharmas as they truly are;
the syllable *kṣa* refers to entering into the moment-to-moment arising and ceasing of all dharmas.
Because it is inexhaustible, indestructible, and primordially quiescent;
the meaning of these eight characters can be known and entered.
This is called the meaning of the initial entry.
This dharani method is collectively named "Having Written," which one should receive and uphold; this is the second entry into the meaning.
This method is collectively named "Recitation and Recollection Every Half-Month," which one should recite and remember every half-month; this is the third entry into the meaning.
A bodhisattva should, by means of this dhāraṇī, instruct, praise, and gladden others;
this is the fourth entry into the meaning.
Śāriputra, by means of these four dharmas...
To cause the bodhisattvas to attain this dhāraṇī,
the Buddha spoke these verses (gāthā):
"Writing it down and upholding it, and contemplating [it]— these are the eight superior characters."
Constantly practicing recitation for half a month, one teaches and transforms all sentient beings and draws near to the unsurpassed path. In the realm of supreme wisdom,
one constantly beholds all Tathāgatas and also hears them preach the wondrous Dharma.
If there are bodhisattvas who receive and uphold dhāraṇīs,
they obtain four merits. What are these four?
The World-Honored Buddhas of the ten directions constantly protect and keep them in mind;
they shall not be obstructed by the King of Māras,
and all evils of body, speech, and mind will be completely eliminated.
One attains inexhaustible eloquence.
Śāriputra, if there is a bodhisattva who upholds this dhāraṇī,
they shall obtain these four kinds of merit.
The Buddha spoke this geya:
"Those whom all Buddhas protect and keep in mind cannot be thwarted by any maras;
their three evil karmas are extinguished, and their eloquence in joyful exposition is boundless."
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śāriputra:
"In the distant past, incalculable asaṃkhyeya kalpas ago,
there was a buddha named Ratnaśrīprabharāja Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
Endowed with the ten titles,
he appeared in the world to teach and transform sentient beings.
After this Buddha passed into parinirvāṇa, there was a Wheel-Turning Sage King.
He was named Holder of Radiance and was fully endowed with the seven treasures.
That king had a son named Inconceivable Merit and Auspiciousness,
who was sixteen years of age.
After that Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, upon hearing this dhāraṇī being taught,
they shall for seventy thousand lifetimes neither sleep nor be indolent,
and for seventy thousand lifetimes they shall not crave royal sovereignty.
He did not begrudge his own body, life, or other material possessions.
For seventy thousand lifetimes, he never lay down to sleep but sat continuously in meditation.
He constantly heard the Dharma preached by ninety billion nayutas of Buddhas.
Having heard the Dharma, the Buddha prophesied his renunciation of the world,
stating that after ninety thousand kalpas he would attain a dhāraṇī named "Taking the Boundless Gate. Having attained it,
he would explain it for the sake of sentient beings throughout the course of a single lifetime.
He will teach and transform eighty billion hundred thousand nayutas of sentient beings,
causing them to abide in the stage of non-retrogression and enabling them to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, there was among the assembly a son of a householder named Candracchattra.
Having heard from him the exposition of the *Anantamukhapraveśadhāraṇī*,
he rejoiced upon hearing it.
By virtue of this merit of sympathetic joy, you shall receive the prediction of enlightenment from nine hundred million billion Buddhas.
You shall be the foremost among those who uphold dhāraṇīs;
all sentient beings who hear what you preach shall love and delight in it.
No one shall be able to defeat you in debate or challenge.
In a future age, after three *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas have passed,
you shall teach and transform all sentient beings so that they all attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Śāriputra, what do you think?
Was that Prince of Inconceivable Merit and Virtue at that time anyone else?
He was none other than the Buddha Amitāyus.
The son of the elder Candravrata was that very Buddha Dīpaṃkara.
Śāriputra, in the past, I and the various bodhisattvas heard this dhāraṇī being taught; having heard it, we rejoiced accordingly.
By means of these roots of goodness, for four million kalpas one shall not be born in the evil destinies.
Therefore, Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva mahāsattva desires to swiftly attain awakening, [they should practice this].
One should rejoice in this *Anantamukha-parigraha-dhāraṇī* and apply oneself with diligent effort.
Why? Because when a bodhisattva achieves and abides in the stage of non-retrogression, they shall attain *sambodhi*.
How much more so for those who write it down, read it, recite it, uphold it, explain it, and elucidate it!
Except for the Buddhas, no one is able to describe the limit of these merits.
The Buddha spoke this geya.
Innumerable kalpas ago, there appeared in the world the Tathāgata Ratnaketu,
who transformed sentient beings; after that Buddha had entered parinirvāṇa, bringing immeasurable benefit, there was a Wheel-Turning Sage King.
The son’s name was Guṇakīrti; at the age of sixteen,
after the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata, upon hearing this dhāraṇī being preached,
he remained free from sleep and indolence for seventy thousand lifetimes.
Without craving for wealth, royal rank, or even life itself,
they were able to hear and receive with a single mind the wondrous Dharma-gates spoken by ninety billion nayutas of Buddhas.
The Tathāgata then gave him this prediction: "After ninety thousand worlds have passed, he shall attain the dharma of dhāraṇī named 'Taking Up Boundless Gates.
Having attained it, he shall preach it for others, benefiting countless multitudes."
They were all caused to abide in non-retrogression from unsurpassed *samyak-saṃbodhi*.
When the elder’s son Candracchattra heard the teaching of the *dhāraṇī*,
he gave rise to the merit of sympathetic joy (*anumodanā*), and all the Buddhas conferred upon him a prophecy (*vyākaraṇa*).
You have received this dhāraṇī, which is the most supreme;
if you explain it to others, there will be none who do not rejoice in it.
If anyone should pose difficult questions or challenges, none shall be able to defeat you.
In a future age, after three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* have passed, you shall attain the Unsurpassed Way;
the sentient beings whom you are to transform are those very ones.
The son of a householder named Candracchattra was indeed the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara.
The Dharma teacher who previously expounded this is none other than Amitāyus Buddha.
I and all the bodhisattvas have heard this dhāraṇī in the past;
for four million kalpas, we shall not be born into any of the evil realms.
If a bodhisattva wishes to attain the unsurpassed, all-encompassing knowledge of the path, they should practice with diligent vigor and rejoice in this dhāraṇī. Why is this so?
Because it causes one to abide in the stage of non-retrogression.
If one can rejoice [in this merit], their virtue is already such as this;
how much more so for those who copy, read, recite, and explain its meaning!
Suppose there were the seven treasures filling worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—
The merit of such giving cannot be compared; therefore,
the wise person should apply themselves with diligent vigor to receive and uphold this dhāraṇī in order to seek the unsurpassed path.
Śāriputra, if a bodhisattva receives and maintains this dhāraṇī,
there are eight yakṣas dwelling on the Snowy Mountains who will protect them day and night to increase their lifespan.
What are the eight?
They are the valiant yakṣa and the steadfast yakṣa.
The Yakṣa Īśvara, the Yakṣa Nārāyaṇabala, and the Yakṣa Dharmaprayoga.
The Yakṣa Abandhya, the Yakṣa Jambha, and the Yakṣa Supakṣa.
Śāriputra, these eight yakṣas will constantly protect those who receive and uphold this dhāraṇī.
If one bathes cleanly and puts on newly dyed robes, [they shall guard them].
One should constantly practice walking meditation,
harbor no intent to harm any sentient being,
and always contemplate this dharani method within oneself.
Those yakṣas shall swiftly come to provide protection.
Furthermore, there are eight great bodhisattvas who dwell in the desire realm heavens;
they shall likewise guard and keep in mind those who receive and uphold this dhāraṇī.
Their names were Bodhisattva Radiance,
Bodhisattva Wisdom Radiance,
and Bodhisattva Solar Radiance.
He taught and transformed the Bodhisattvas,
causing the Bodhisattva Sarvārthasiddhi and the Bodhisattva Maheśvara to fulfill all their intentions.
The Bodhisattva Śuddharāja,
the Bodhisattva Cāritramati,
and those other bodhisattvas had attained dhāraṇīs.
If a bodhisattva attains dhāraṇī, they shall fulfill their true vows and recognize the kindness [of the Dharma].
If a bodhisattva maintains dhāraṇī, they shall attain the true Dharma and share it with all sentient beings.
If a bodhisattva upholds this dhāraṇī, they shall be fully endowed with merit and achieve profound wisdom.
The Buddha taught this Dharma to three hundred thousand billion nayutas of bodhisattvas.
Having attained this "Dhāraṇī of the Gate of Boundless Appropriation," they shall not regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Eight *vibhara* numbers of devas and humans [shall likewise attain it].
They resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, what is the name of this sutra?"
"How should it be received and upheld?
The Buddha told Śāriputra,
"This sūtra is named the *Dhāraṇī of the Gate of Taking Up the Infinite*."
You should receive and uphold it;
it is also called "the exclusive practice of Bodhisattvas.
You should receive and uphold it.
It is also called "Eliminating All Māras";
you should uphold it.
It is also called "Attaining All-Knowledge."
"You should receive and uphold it. At that time, Śāriputra and all the bodhisattvas,
along with the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth, [did so].
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Śāriputra Dhāraṇī Sūtra.
